flashcards.q: What does each of transformers, datasets, tokenizers, accelerate, peft, and trl actually do?
flashcards.a: transformers = uniform model/tokenizer interface. datasets = Arrow-backed, memory-mapped/streamable data loading. tokenizers = fast Rust tokenization backend. accelerate = topology-agnostic training launch + mixed precision. peft = parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA). trl = post-training trainers (SFT/DPO/GRPO) built on the rest.

flashcards.q: Explain LoRA's parameter math and why it drastically cuts trainable parameters.
flashcards.a: LoRA freezes W and learns ΔW=BA where B is d×r, A is r×k, r≪d,k. Trainable params = r(d+k) instead of d·k. For a 4096×4096 matrix with r=16: ~131K params vs 16.8M full, over 100x fewer.

flashcards.q: What does QLoRA add on top of LoRA, and why does it matter?
flashcards.a: QLoRA loads the frozen base model in 4-bit quantization (NF4, plus double quantization of quant constants) and trains LoRA adapters in higher precision on top. This makes fine-tuning a 70B model feasible on a single 48-80GB GPU instead of needing multiple 80GB GPUs for full-precision fine-tuning.

flashcards.q: Why is a pickle-based .bin checkpoint a security risk that safetensors eliminates?
flashcards.a: Pickle serializes instructions for reconstructing arbitrary Python objects, including calls to arbitrary callables — deserializing can execute code. Safetensors stores only a header (names/shapes/dtypes/offsets) plus raw tensor bytes, with no executable content possible by the format's construction.

flashcards.q: What is the current (as of Dec 2025) status of Hugging Face's TGI, and what does HF recommend instead?
flashcards.a: TGI entered maintenance mode in December 2025 — only minor bug fixes and doc updates accepted. HF's own documentation recommends vLLM and SGLang for new production serving.

flashcards.q: What does device_map="auto" actually do, and which library implements it?
flashcards.a: It's an accelerate feature exposed through transformers: accelerate inspects available GPU/CPU/disk memory, computes a layer-to-device assignment, and inserts hooks so activations move across device boundaries transparently during the forward pass.

flashcards.q: Contrast datasets' memory-mapped mode with streaming mode.
flashcards.a: Memory-mapped (default): backed by a local Arrow file, gives full random access (ds[i], .shuffle(), cached .map()) but needs the file on local disk. Streaming: no local materialization, iterates directly, but only supports buffer-based approximate shuffling, no true random access.

flashcards.q: Why should you always pin an explicit revision hash when loading a model from the Hub in production?
flashcards.a: Without pinning, from_pretrained(..., revision="main") resolves to whatever the repo owner most recently pushed. A production system can silently start loading different weights or tokenizer behavior after a cold start or cache eviction with zero code change on your side.

SFT: supervised next-token training on instruction/response pairs. DPO: closed-form training directly on preference pairs (chosen vs rejected), no separate reward model or rollouts. GRPO: RL using group-relative advantage from sampled completions, needs a verifiable reward (math/code correctness), underlies DeepSeek-R1-style reasoning post-training.

flashcards.q: Where does LangChain genuinely earn its place versus where senior teams now skip it?
flashcards.a: Earns it: complex multi-provider orchestration, and specifically LangGraph for durable checkpointed multi-agent state. Skipped by seniors: LCEL beyond simple linear chains, LangChain's memory abstractions (teams roll their own), and the vector-store wrapper layer once committed to one DB's native client.

flashcards.q: What's the 2026 pattern for teams with 5+ engineers on LLM features moving off LangChain?
flashcards.a: Provider SDK calls directly, LiteLLM for cross-provider routing, and Pydantic for schema validation — because model providers converged enough by 2026 that the abstraction no longer hides much real complexity, while adding 15-40 frame debugging stack traces.

flashcards.q: Why is saving a PEFT/LoRA adapter so much smaller than the base model, and why does that matter for serving?
flashcards.a: save_pretrained on a PEFT model saves only the adapter weights (tens to low-hundreds of MB), not the frozen base (which can be 100+ GB). This is why serving many fine-tuned variants of one base model is cheap — vLLM's multi-LoRA serving loads the base once and swaps adapters per request.

flashcards.q: What real-world incident illustrates the danger of trust_remote_code=True?
flashcards.a: CVE-2026-6859: InstructLab hardcoded trust_remote_code=True, meaning a specially crafted malicious model uploaded to the Hub could achieve remote code execution on any user who loaded it — independent of whether the checkpoint format itself was safetensors or pickle.
